name: Volcanic & aviation ash
value: No red aviation codes found (18 Nov)
summary: No red aviation codes, VEI 4+ eruptions or ash-related airspace closures found as of 18 Nov; Mayon at alert level 3
state: Mayon in the Philippines remains at alert level 3 after a moderately explosive eruption on 30 Oct sent ash about 3,000 metres above the crater; pilots are told to avoid the summit, but no flight cancellations were reported (Nature World News, 4 Nov). Searches on 18 Nov found no red aviation colour code near major air routes, no VEI 4+ eruption and no major ash-related airspace closure. Ongoing eruptions remain local hazards, so the signal stays Normal.
for_you: No volcanic ash disruption to flights was found. Travellers to the Philippines or Indonesia can check airline notices and FCDO travel advice for areas near active volcanoes.
rubric_hit: Normal: no aviation colour code red and no large eruption found as of 18 Nov

sources.title: Nature World News — Mayon volcano stays alert level 3 as lava flows and new ash plumes follow explosive eruption

why: Major eruptions ground flights (Iceland 2010) and can cool the climate for years.
drivers: Volcanic unrest; impact depends on ash plume height and jet-stream direction.

rubric.alert: Major airspace closures from ash, or a VEI 4+ eruption.
